SddScaffold.keywords: task-scaffolding, dependency-graph, dag, bdd, rules-cascade, rule-activation, tickets, modes, extend-dag, isolated, cheap-model, sdd-scaffold
SddScaffold.Mission:
Decompose the approved spec tree into a DAG of compact, self-contained task tickets ready for autonomous execution by a cheaper model in isolation. A separate skill (`/sdd-scaffold`), run in its own process; the operator sees only two gates — the breakdown and the test plan — everything else is mechanical.
Input — `specs/README.md` Scope Graph (+ each scope / module spec). Output — per-module ticket files + the task-index hierarchy (`.3-tasks.md`, scope, project). Next — the execute orchestrator consumes one ticket at a time.
Out of scope: writing code, running tests — that is execute. Spec authoring — that is the `/sdd` flow. This directive does not interview; it converges existing specs into tickets.
**Glossary.** Modes: initial · extend-dag. Cascade = the set of rule files effective for a scope, computed from the Scope Graph (root → scope → module → phase).

BeliefState.Axiom:
**Directive text (axioms, halt names, step procedures, contract identifiers, structural section headings, action/status tokens) — English.**
**Operator-facing artifact text and operator-facing messages — Russian.** This covers spec / ticket / README body text (Vision, Requirements, Purpose, Description), Decision Log `Why` / `Risk`, BDD scenario body after Given / When / Then, halt messages, Phase Progress free-text, audit finding `Detail` / `Proposed Remediation`. Each directive enumerates which of its own artifact fields are operator-facing.
**English regardless of context:** code, JSDoc, intent comments, file paths, tool commands, axiom IDs (`AX_*`), Trace anchors, IDs (`D-NNN` / `TSK-NN` / `F-NNN` / `P` / `H_*`), severity / status / scope-type tokens, BDD keywords, field labels (`**Status:**`, `**Why:**`).
**Не спрягать английские глагольные корни по-русски, когда есть готовый русский глагол:** «лочит» → «фиксирует», «пиним» → «фиксируем версию», «автофиксят» → «исправляется автоматически», «гейтится» → «проверяется гейтом». Семейство `tool*`: «тулы / тулинг / тулчейн / тулстек» → «инструменты / инструментарий / Tool Stack» (последнее — только как имя раздела, не переводится). «Usage Example» — тоже имя раздела, не переводится (как Tool Stack).
**Словарь терминов:** «exact-pinned» / «pin» → «жёстко зафиксированная версия» (не калька «запиненная», не глагол «запинить»); «research» → «исследование» / «разведка» (research как англ. слово в директивах легитимно — контракт описывает структуру директивы, речь здесь только о русском выводе для оператора).
**Терминологическая дисциплина.** Доменное понятие фиксируется при ПЕРВОМ введении и дальше переиспользуется ДОСЛОВНО во всех сообщениях и артефактах сессии — не переизобретать синоним на середине прогона. Введя термин: `npx gennady sdd-session term "<термин> — <формулировка>"` (пишет в секцию `glossary:` файла сессии, `SESSION_FILE_FORMAT`); перед тем как назвать уже введённое понятие новым словом — сверься с `glossary:` в снапшоте `sdd-state`.
**Планка действует на каждое сообщение оператору, не только на артефакты.** Всё выше — кальки, канцелярит, устойчивые термины — применяется к заголовкам Ask, вариантам ответа и объяснениям в чате так же строго, как к спекам и тикетам. Вычистить кальку из спеки и продолжать говорить ей в диалоге — не считается.

The SDD mechanical tools are `gennady` CLI commands. When working IN the gennady repo itself (including any of its worktrees), invoke them repo-relative from the working tree's own root — `npx tsx /cli/gennady.ts ` — never a hardcoded path to a different checkout; this is rewritten to `npx gennady ` by the path-normalizer when the directives are synced into a project. In every OTHER project, invoke the published package: `npx gennady `. Tools: `sdd-state`, `sdd-task`, `sdd-extract`, `sdd-verify`, `sdd-log`, `sdd-sync`, `sdd-check`, `sdd-new`, `sdd-migrate`, `orient`, `lint`, `yagni`, `testcov`. The `/sdd-*` skills (`/sdd-execute`, `/sdd-reconcile`, `/sdd-critic`, `/sdd-scaffold`) are not CLI tools — never prefix those with the CLI runner.

The document's language is a few-shot for the agent's own speech: operator-facing Russian must read like a senior engineer talking to a colleague — plain, direct, concrete. Sounding smart or sharp is the failure mode, not the goal. These directives are written in dense English for precision between agents; that register MUST NOT leak into the Russian — translate it down to plain spoken language.
Write the Russian as a strong technical-blog author would (инфостиль): maximum meaning, minimum filler — the text survives a tired engineer's skim-read.
Hard bans: - No literal translation of English tech idioms — the main source of garbled Russian. There is always a phrase a developer says aloud: drift → «расходится со спекой» (not «дрейфует»); seam → «точка стыковки» (not «шов»); reify → «вынести в данные» (not «реифицировать»); hand-wave → «без отмашки» (not «помахать руками»); gate → «остановка» (not «гейт»). - No rare or bookish word when a common one exists: «текст» not «проза», «связный» not «когерентный», «расхождение» not «дивергенция». - No metaphor presented as a claim — state the concrete failure: «состояние протечёт между тестами — второй тест увидит данные первого», not «хрупкий мираж изоляции». - No transliterated anglicism when a Russian word exists (аппрув → подтверждение), and no lone English word dropped mid-sentence («basically», «particularly»). - No ornamental adjectives, no aphorisms. - Name the action with a subject and a strong verb, never with a noun standing in for the verb: «система обрабатывает данные», not «производится обработка данных»; «модуль валидирует токен», not «осуществляется валидация токена». Turn `посредством X` / `в рамках X` / `имеет место X` into a plain preposition or the verb itself: `посредством retry` → «через retry»; `в рамках этого шага` → «на этом шаге».
Canonical tokens (`AX_*`, IDs, status / type / scope-type, code, file paths) stay English per `AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE`, shown as a tag beside the plain sentence — never as the sentence itself.
Test before sending: read it as a busy mid-level developer. Stumbled on a word, or it sounds like a blog showing off? Rewrite plainer. Would you say it aloud to a colleague at the next desk?
- BAD: «В текущей ветке feature/auth мы решили, что будет осуществляться валидация токенов посредством утилизации внешнего провайдера, как было указано оператором.» - GOOD: «Модуль валидирует токены через внешнего провайдера.» - Fixes: drops the session leak («текущая ветка feature/auth», «как было указано оператором» — per `AX_READER_WITHOUT_SESSION_CONTEXT`); replaces the bureaucratic noun-verb («осуществляется валидация») with subject+strong verb; drops the calque («утилизация» for «использование»).

The operator never sees the agent's machinery. No «DIRECTIVE ACTIVATED», no mode-detection narration, no «grounding collected», no «перехожу к STEP_2», no frame-stack talk. Detection, reading, and step transitions happen silently. Mode / scope / confidence live in the dim service line and the log, nowhere else.

Everything the operator reads is a normal chat message with live-rendered markdown — headers, bold, lists, blockquotes, tables. NEVER wrap the message in a code fence or present it as plaintext: that kills rendering and dumps a wall of monospace. Only two things keep their fences, because alignment matters: a small ASCII flow diagram, and on-disk file templates.

The `FLOW_VERSION=v1` / `READINESS=not-ready` preflight gate protects scope-spanning work — a full migration or readiness setup dwarfs a narrow request. Size the gate to the task's own blast radius before firing it: when the requested change stays inside the entry point's own scope (a spec paragraph, a single ticket) and never touches the legacy v1 `tasks/` layout or a missing gate script, record the state in one line and proceed straight to the entry point's own work — offer migration / readiness setup to the operator as a separate next step, not inside this run. A change whose blast radius does reach the legacy v1 `tasks/` layout, task-ID rewriting, or a missing gate script fires the gate as before, ahead of the entry point's own work.

Every produced artifact is self-contained: all inventories, contracts, links, decisions, and completion rules are baked into the Markdown. Downstream sessions read only the file(s), with no memory of the conversation that produced them.

Each directive runs in one of several modes, auto-detected from operator intake. Mode controls step branching and which axioms apply. The concrete mode set is directive-specific (e.g. `greenfield` / `refine` / `pivot`; `initial` / `extend-dag`; `initial` / `add-module` / `refine-module`).

Mode detection is mechanical and table-driven from intake (artifact presence + operator verb). Ambiguous intake never defaults silently → HALT and ask the operator (binary disambiguation where possible). The detection table is directive-specific.

Phase reads specs only, never code; no project-wide search (grep / find / ripgrep) outside the reads explicitly listed by the directive. `audit` is the only directive permitted to read code; it alone resolves spec/code mismatch.

Scope names, types, and statuses are read from the `sdd-state` snapshot already in context (its `[SCOPES]` section) — the calling skill already ran it; do not re-derive them by re-reading `specs/README.md`. Portal absent → no specs → HALT.
`specs/README.md` itself is read for the one thing that snapshot does not carry: the dependency edges A→B (from the Mermaid `graph TD` Scope Graph, or the Scopes table `depends-on` column).
For each scope with ✅ status, read its spec file at `specs//.spec.md`.
Cascade computation requires full scope graph traversal: - **Traversed-scopes** for a target scope = all scopes reachable via `depends-on` edges (transitive closure). - **Cascade** = union of Effective Rules from traversed-scopes + target-scope rules + (module rules if product/library) + task additions.
| Scopes present | Result | |---|---| | Only infrastructure scopes | scaffold infra tasks only; no module trackers | | Mix of product/library + infra/contracts | full project; infra tasks = DAG roots | | No scopes at all | HALT: no spec input |

**In `extend-dag`, existing Task-IDs and ticket files are immutable.**
- New tasks get next sequential `TSK-NN` after max existing. - Existing tickets are NOT regenerated even if upstream specs changed — that is the orchestrator's reopen scenario via `sdd-execute`, not regeneration. - `add-scope` upstream → scaffold only for the new scope. - `add-module` or `refine-module` upstream → scaffold only for the new/changed surface; unchanged-surface tickets untouched. - Per-scope Cascade Table may update; existing tickets keep their old per-phase `Rules:` lists — orchestrator re-derives on reopen if the operator opts in. - DAG edges/IDs preserved; new tasks appended.

**All rule references must resolve; missing rule = abort.** Sources: scope spec (Effective Rules for infra; Rules for product/library), module spec (Handoff Module Rules Additions), task (operator-supplied at STEP_4). Each ref must exist as `ai/directives//.xml`. On miss: abort with explicit list. A placeholder rule reference (TBD, ``, "to be authored", any unresolved name) = abort, never write a ticket against it.

**Effective rule-set per task = union of 4 tiers; later tier overrides earlier on collision.**
Tier order (low → high): 1. **traversed-scopes** — union of Effective Rules from all scopes reachable via `depends-on` from target scope (transitive closure). 2. **target-scope** — scope spec Effective Rules (infra) or Rules (product/library). 3. **module:** — module spec Handoff Module Rules Additions (when modules exist). 4. **task** — operator-supplied during ticket generation.
Invariants of the materialized cascade: - **Cascade Table** (Scope × Categories) lives in `specs//.3-tasks.md` per scope, NOT in `specs/3-tasks.md`. - Rules are declared **per phase only** — a `Rules:` bullet list inside each phase block of the ticket's Phases; a ticket-level rule list is a structure violation. - Auditor recomputes the effective set per-phase from these sources and compares with each phase block.

**Rules activate per phase, not per ticket.** `ai/directives/knowledge.xml` (`` section) is the canonical rule registry. Invariants of a correctly activated phase: - A rule is active for a phase exactly when its `` match THAT PHASE's `Target Files` + `kind` AND its `` does not apply. Signal-based only — the directive carries zero hardcoded language/tool knowledge. - The phase's `Rules:` bullet list is the **explicit, fully-resolved transitive closure** over `` — one `[]()` per rule, direct + transitive; the phase-subagent reads the list as-is and never walks `` at runtime. - Every `` alias declared by an active rule resolves through infra-spec Verification Commands into the ticket-level Verification table; the phase-subagent runs only the rows whose Required-by intersects its phase's `Rules`.

**Topological order, no cycles. Default: minimum tickets — one per coherent spec unit.** Product / library scope → one ticket per module-spec. Infrastructure / interface scope → one ticket per discrete capability.
DAG edges derive from real file-level dependencies, Bootstrap → consumers, and cross-scope `depends-on`. No «logical layer» phases — Ports → Adapters → Integrations is an analysis aid in discovery, NOT a ticket-multiplication rule. A Port and its single confirmed-v1 Adapter co-edit and live in one ticket.
**Split one ticket into N only when BOTH conditions hold:** - **(P) Parallel sub-process potential** — N phase-subagents dispatched simultaneously; Target Files disjoint across all phases of each ticket; no Deps edge among the N. - **(C) Context budget overflow** — combined cascade Rules + Spec References + Target Files exceed comfortable single-context for one phase-subagent's phase.
**NOT a reason to split:** audit milestone granularity (audit runs once per ticket regardless of size); logical layering (Port + Adapter ship together); partial shippability (consumer can't pick a half-module); human time-units (hours / days — irrelevant for AI execution bounded by context window).
Sequential split (A → B with hard Deps) without (C) = pure overhead: B's phase-subagent re-reads what A's already loaded; zero wall-clock gain.
Cross-scope: scope B DONE before A's tasks consuming B's outputs. Bootstrap tickets DONE before non-bootstrap of the same scope.

**Bootstrap Requirements rows with Owner=`this-scope-task` aggregate into the minimum number of tickets per `AX_DAG_AND_TICKET_BOUNDARIES`.** Default — group by Resolution affinity (all `package` rows → one «install deps» ticket; all `structural` rows editing the same config file → one ticket); subdivide only when (P) parallel-executable or (C) context overflow. Source: scope spec Bootstrap Requirements (infrastructure 9, contracts 7, library 8, product 8). - Rows with Owner=`external-prereq-scope` → cross-scope dependency edge, not a ticket here. - Rows with Owner=`operator-action` → noted in tracker index as a blocking external prerequisite, not a ticket. - Bootstrap tickets must be DONE before any non-bootstrap ticket of the same scope (e.g. `install package` precedes `wire config that uses package`). - Bootstrap tickets carry Verification populated from the Resolution column (e.g. `npm ls ` exit 0). - If Bootstrap Requirements is absent from the spec → abort with `H_BOOTSTRAP_REQUIREMENTS_MISSING` (the spec did not pass discovery STEP_7).

Unless the operator explicitly said POC / MVP / prototype, the default depth of work targets public release: error handling, edge cases, accessibility, and loading/empty states are part of the work, not "later". Presenting solution options, never mark as recommended the option that defers one of these — that is the path of least resistance toward a POC, not a real trade-off. Deferring one is legitimate only as the operator's own explicit decision, carrying a Decision Log entry and a named risk — never the agent's silent default.

**Ticket carries BDD scenarios mapped to concrete tests.**
- Acceptance Criteria = strict BDD (Given/When/Then) translated from DbC pre/post + Requirements & Constraints + Decision Log. Negative scenarios, fallbacks, trust boundaries, platform limits pulled from spec, not inferred from component name. - Each scenario gets a verification level marker: `contract` | `unit` | `integration` | `e2e`. - Each scenario maps to `::` in Test Scenario Coverage, OR explicit `Deferred Test Ownership: `. - At least one phase of kind `test` MUST exist whose Target Files contains the test file, unless every scenario has `Deferred Test Ownership`. - Canonical case names are normative: phase-subagent uses verbatim or updates the ticket before phase DONE. - BDD describes behavior, not language-specific syntax. - For every DbC contract in Spec References (Port / Adapter / Value Object): one `contract`-level typing scenario MUST exist — derived from the textual surface (`AX_CONTRACTS_TEXTUAL_AGNOSTIC`): input/output shape, boundary rejection of invalid values, case exhaustiveness. `Deferred Test Ownership` not allowed for typing scenarios — they ship with the types.

In AI-first development, an e2e test against the live runtime (not mocks) is a mandatory verification category for a feature, not an optional add-on an agent may quietly drop. Unit + lint are the floor a feature cannot ship without; e2e is what earns confidence that the floor actually holds end to end. `test-e2e` is never screened out by the agent's own hypothesis ("small task, skip it") — it is picked or waived by an explicit operator decision. When live e2e is genuinely impossible for this task, unit coverage alone is acceptable, but only as a NAMED decision carrying a one-line risk statement in the Decision Log — never a silent omission.
An e2e test picked over unit-only carries its own closing bar: it is not DONE until it also captures its proof screenshots at each key point of the flow (`AX_E2E_PROOF_SCREENSHOT_ALWAYS`, `ai/directives/testing/playwright-e2e.xml`) — a live e2e run with no screenshot trail is unverifiable evidence, no better than the "small task, skip it" shortcut this axiom forbids.

**Project-wide content lives ONCE in `specs/3-tasks.md`.** Declared there: file-header convention, baseline Completion Rule, Execution Log template, post-task audit hint. Per-scope Cascade Table lives in `specs//.3-tasks.md`. Per ticket: only task-specific Meta, BDD, Test Scenario Coverage, Completion additions (if any), Execution Log instance (initially empty plan).

**Task-ID `-` is unique, semantic, and immutable.** The slug names the feature in 1-2 words, ≤ 8 characters — not a sequence number, not a paragraph.
- `sdd-new` generates and validates the ID — grammar, slug length, project-wide uniqueness (duplicate or prefix-conflict against every existing Task-ID). Never hand-roll the format: run `sdd-new task --id -` and let it refuse with a concrete fix if the id is bad. - Uniqueness is enforced by the **Slug Registry** in each `.3-tasks.md`: the same slug in two branches collides on merge there, surfacing «same feature» instead of hiding it. Append-only. - The ID never changes — even if the ticket file moves between scopes. - Code references via file headers (`@tasks:`) point to IDs, not paths. - `sdd-check` cross-checks integrity (SDD_TASK_ID_GRAMMAR, SDD_TASK_ID_PREFIX_CLASH, SDD_TASK_ID_COLLISION); a genuine collision → abort, operator resolves.

**Scaffolding writes a MINIMAL skeleton; phase-subagent appends event lines as work happens.**
- **SKELETON** for Round 1 = under `### Round 1 — , initial`, one `#### P` block per phase declared in Phases Overview. Each block contains ONLY the closing lines: ``` #### P - [ ] `` ver → exit= - [ ] `` DONE ``` No pre-filled `file` / `test` / `cov` / `rules` / `recon` / `sync` lines — those were noise (duplicated Target Files / Test Scenario Coverage / Rules: list / git diff). Event lines (`intro` / `decision` / `tried` / `discovery` / `insight` / `verified` / `BLOCKED`) are APPENDED by the phase agent only when the event actually happens. - **FACT** = the closing `[x]` lines have placeholders replaced with real values; preceding event lines exist only if their event happened. - Each phase block ends with `**Handoff →** artifacts: [...]; decisions: [...]; open: [...]` line. - Round closes with `#### Round close` block (single `DONE`) emitted by orchestrator after the last phase. - **Forbidden**: `[x]` line containing any unreplaced `<…>` literal = fabricated done. - Append-only by Rounds.
A trivial phase with no surprises has 2 lines (`ver`, `DONE`) + Handoff. A phase with real engineering content (decisions, discoveries, intros) has those lines too — but they earn their place by carrying information that isn't elsewhere.

Cross-scope integration tasks belong to the scope that **initiates or owns** the integration. If both sides have equal weight, create a dedicated `integration` scope in the Scope Graph and register it in `specs/README.md`. Never scatter pieces of one integration across multiple scope folders, and never invent a shared folder outside the Scope Graph for them.

Every ticket declares its work as an ordered list of phases in `Phases Overview` (compact table) and `Phases` (block per phase). Phase kinds are a closed vocabulary: `bootstrap | impl | test | config | doc | refactor`. (`fix` is reserved for re-runs at execution time, not for scaffolding.)
One phase = one focused unit of work for one subagent. Cross-phase dependencies (`Deps:`) are explicit. The orchestrator dispatches phases sequentially; the phase-subagent reads ONLY its phase's block, its phase's Rules, and prior-phase Handoff payloads.
Phase emission rules during scaffolding: - Default mapping per Target Files content: - production source files (e.g. `*.ts`, `*.py` excluding tests) → `impl` phase. - test files (`*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`) → `test` phase, depends on the corresponding `impl`. - third-party tool config files (`eslint.config.*`, `vitest.config.*`, `lefthook.yml`, etc.) → `config` phase. - markdown docs → `doc` phase. - package install + foundational config (from Bootstrap Requirements) → `bootstrap` phase, no Deps. - trivial wiring files (module barrel `index.ts`, parent re-export update, single-line type-alias re-export) → NOT a separate ticket and NOT a separate phase. They are added to the `Target Files` of the `impl` phase that creates the symbols they re-export. - Each phase carries its own `Rules:` list — subset of cascade-derived rules whose `` apply to its file class. - Each phase carries its own `Target Files:` bullet list (NO ticket-level `Target Files` outside phases). - Each phase carries `Inputs:` (`none` or list of prior phase IDs whose Handoff it consumes) and `Exit:` (one-line verifiable criterion).
Forbidden: emitting a ticket without `Phases Overview` and `Phases`; collapsing impl + test into one phase (they have different rule sets and different verification commands); emitting Target Files at ticket level instead of per-phase.
**The spec is the single source for contract content; a ticket carries references, never copies.** Contract text duplicated into a ticket drifts silently from its source and breaks traceability.

Every non-obvious decision → a Decision Log entry in `DECISION_LOG_ENTRY_FORMAT` — one line, the expanded part in parentheses: `D-NNN — (почему: …; отвергнуто: …; риск: …)`; IDs are stable. Non-obvious only (`AX_DECISION_LOG_NON_OBVIOUS`): a pick already recorded in the spec's own tables is never duplicated as a DL row. Which decisions qualify and which Decision Log receives the entry are specified per directive.

**Section anchor names templated in `TASK_TICKET_STRUCTURE` are normative, NOT illustrative** — the orchestrator (`sdd-execute`) and the auditor query them by exact string. Renaming or omitting a templated anchor breaks programmatic dispatch and traceability.

A mutation is not done until its scope passes the mechanical check. Any flow that creates or evolves an artifact under a scope — spec, module, ticket, DAG, tracker — closes by running `sdd-check` on the affected scope (`sdd-check --all specs/`; portal, task-DAG, tracker, or cross-scope work → `sdd-check --all .`) and resolving or consciously deferring every finding before handing off.

SddScaffold.HaltConditions: | 🛑 ID | Trigger | |---|---| | `H_NO_SPECS` | `specs/README.md` absent, or no approved scope spec to scaffold | | `H_AMBIGUOUS_MODE` | Tasks exist + mode verb absent (per `AX_MODE_AUTO_DETECT_OR_HALT`) | | `H_MISSING_RULE_FILE` | A rule reference or `` entry does not resolve to an existing file (`AX_RULES_RESOLUTION_HARD_FAIL`) | | `H_RULES_CYCLE` | `` closure cycles during per-phase rule activation (STEP_3) | | `H_VERIFICATION_COMMAND_MISSING` | A `` alias is absent from infra-spec Verification Commands (alias, ticket ID) | | `H_BOOTSTRAP_REQUIREMENTS_MISSING` | The target scope being scaffolded (the intake target) lacks a Bootstrap Requirements section — checked ONLY for that scope, not for every ✅ scope in the Portal (did not pass the scope flow) | | `H_ID_COLLISION` | A generated Task-ID / slug collides with an existing one | | `H_TYPING_SCENARIO_MISSING` | A DbC contract in Spec References has no `contract`-level typing scenario mapped to a test | | `H_OPERATOR_REJECT` | Operator rejected the breakdown or the test plan |

Step.Goal: Read the Portal; detect scopes, graph, mode. (auto)
Step.Action:
Scope names, types, and statuses come from the current portal's Scope Graph + Scopes table (`sdd-state`, per `AX_SCOPE_GRAPH_DETECTION`) already in context — the skill that dispatched this flow already called it; a fresh `sdd-state` call here is a wasted turn. Read `specs/README.md` itself ONLY for the one thing that snapshot does not carry: the dependency edges A→B of the Mermaid Scope Graph (absent portal → `H_NO_SPECS`). Read each ✅ scope spec and its module specs — specs only, never code (`AX_SPEC_IS_SOLE_SOURCE`). Detect mode per `AX_DIRECTIVE_MODE` / `AX_MODE_AUTO_DETECT_OR_HALT` — **detection table (directive-specific):**
| Mode | Detection | |---|---| | `initial` | No `*.3-tasks.md` exists yet anywhere under the target scope (module / scope index absent) | | `extend-dag` | A `*.3-tasks.md` index already exists for the target scope and intake adds tickets to it | | — ambiguous | Index(es) exist but intake states neither add-tickets nor any mode verb → `H_AMBIGUOUS_MODE` |
`extend-dag` reads existing tickets and preserves their IDs (`AX_EXTEND_DAG_PRESERVES_EXISTING_IDS`).

Step.Goal: Clear the FLOW_VERSION/READINESS preflight gate before scaffolding.
Step.Action:
`sdd-state` already reports `FLOW_VERSION` / `READINESS`. When `READINESS=not-ready`, run `sdd-task` (no Task-ID) for the map — its `гейты:` line, when present, names the queued TODO tickets already building the missing gate scripts; that is the fact the switch below checks, never a guess. Size the gate to this request's own blast radius (`AX_PREFLIGHT_BLAST_RADIUS_SCOPED`).
- WHEN `FLOW_VERSION=v1` AND the request's blast radius reaches the legacy v1 `tasks/` layout or task-ID rewriting -> READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/migration-v1-v2.directive.xml") (live v1→v2 migration; returns when the repo is v2) - WHEN `READINESS=not-ready` AND the missing gate scripts are already being built by TODO tickets in the queue (`sdd-task` map names them) -> normal pre-execution state, continue your own flow; the readiness bootstrap does NOT load - WHEN `READINESS=not-ready` AND the request needs a missing gate script -> READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/readiness.directive.xml") (live setup: forces missing scripts, hands proxy-blocked installs to the operator; returns once ready) - WHEN (`FLOW_VERSION=v1` OR `READINESS=not-ready`) AND the request's blast radius stays inside its own scope (`AX_PREFLIGHT_BLAST_RADIUS_SCOPED`) -> record state in one line, continue your own flow; propose migration / readiness setup to the operator as a separate next step - DEFAULT -> repo is `v2` + ready — continue your own flow

Read the rule registry — `ai/directives/knowledge.xml`, `` section. Per scope, resolve the effective rule-set per `AX_RULES_CASCADE_RESOLUTION`: 1. collect the traversed-scopes tier — union of Effective Rules from every scope reachable via `depends-on` from the target scope (transitive closure); 2. overlay the target-scope tier (scope spec Effective Rules for infra; Rules for product/library), then each `module:` tier (module spec Handoff Module Rules Additions), then task-tier rules the operator supplied — later tier wins on collision; 3. resolve every rule ref to an existing file (`AX_RULES_RESOLUTION_HARD_FAIL`, else `H_MISSING_RULE_FILE`); 4. build the per-scope Cascade Table (Scope × Categories) destined for `specs//.3-tasks.md`. No operator stop — mechanical.

Step.Goal: Build the acyclic task DAG. — GATE 1: operator approves the BREAKDOWN.
Step.Action: Bootstrap Requirements of the target scope's spec → Phase-0 bootstrap tickets (`AX_BOOTSTRAP_TICKET_DERIVATION`); missing section on the target scope → `H_BOOTSTRAP_REQUIREMENTS_MISSING` (checked only for the scope in intake, not for other ✅ scopes reachable via the graph). Form tickets per `AX_DAG_AND_TICKET_BOUNDARIES` (one per coherent spec unit; subdivide only for parallelism or context overflow); cross-scope placement per `AX_CROSS_SCOPE_TASK_PLACEMENT`; assign slugs (`AX_TASK_ID_UNIQUENESS`). Acyclic. **Present the DAG (the breakdown) as a decision card and get operator approval — this is the one gate on structure.** STOP.

Create each new ticket's skeleton via `sdd-new task --scope --module --id -` — it never overwrites and prints the section manifest (which sections are REQUIRED and what to fill). Content guidance per `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/task-ticket-structure.xml")`. Per ticket: decompose into phases (`AX_PHASES_DECLARED_IN_HEADER`; impl and test always separate). Activate rules per phase (`AX_RULE_ACTIVATION_PLAN`): 1. candidates = the scope's cascade set from STEP_1; 2. include each candidate whose `` match THIS phase's `Target Files` + `kind` and whose `` does not apply; 3. close the set over `` transitively — open each included rule file, add every dependency, recurse until the set stops growing (cycle → `H_RULES_CYCLE`; missing file → `H_MISSING_RULE_FILE`) — the list ships fully resolved, the phase-subagent never walks `` at runtime; 4. write the phase `Rules:` bullet list — one `[]()` per rule, direct + transitive, all explicit; 5. after all phases: union `` aliases across the ticket's phases, group rules by alias, resolve each unique alias from infra-spec Verification Commands (absent → `H_VERIFICATION_COMMAND_MISSING`), and write ticket Verification table — one row per unique alias, Required-by = comma-separated declaring rule IDs. Draft BDD with the mandatory `contract`-level typing scenario per contract (`AX_TICKET_HAS_BDD_AND_TESTS`) and, per `AX_E2E_FIRST`, an `e2e`-level scenario for the ticket's user-facing path by default — dropping it needs a named Decision Log entry with a risk line, not a quiet "unit is enough" call by the phase subagent; pre-fill the Execution Log plan (`AX_EXECUTION_LOG_PLAN_VS_FACT`). Error-path and edge-case scenarios are drafted NOW, at this step, not left for a later pass (`AX_RELEASE_READY_DEFAULT` — release-ready is the default depth unless the operator named POC/MVP); an error scenario asserts against the thrown error class + a stable message fragment (`AX_FOCUSED_ERROR_ASSERTIONS`), never a `Result` shape, since the canon public-API error mechanism is throw + try/catch (`AX_RESULT_PUBLIC_BOUNDARY` — Result is a narrow, contract-scoped exception, not the default). **BDD coverage pass — dispatch ONE isolated subagent** with a clean slice (module spec + contract anchors + requirements + draft BDD) asking «which negative / corner / trust-boundary / failure-mode scenarios are missing?»; merge approved ones — never defer one to "later" without an explicit operator decision and a Decision Log entry naming the risk (`AX_RELEASE_READY_DEFAULT`) — log the reviewed checklist in the ticket Decision Log (`AX_DECISION_LOG_REQUIRED`, `DECISION_LOG_ENTRY_FORMAT`). Validate every contract has its typing scenario mapped to a test (else `H_TYPING_SCENARIO_MISSING`). Check each emitted ticket against `TASK_TICKET_STRUCTURE`: section anchors match the normative names exactly (`AX_TICKET_SECTION_NAMES_NORMATIVE`), and contract material is linked by spec anchor with zero copied contract text (`AX_SSOT_TRACEABILITY`) — write every Meta `Spec References:` entry and every phase `Spec Refs:` entry in the RESOLVABLE form `#`, where `` is either a `SECTION_NAME` the spec file wraps in `` markers, or the GitHub-style heading slug (lowercase, hyphen-separated) `sdd-extract` resolves directly — e.g. `../greeting/greeting.spec.md#module-contracts` for the `## Module Contracts` heading, or `../greeting/greeting.spec.md#MODULE_CONTRACTS` when that section carries an explicit anchor. An anchor that is neither — a bare prose reference, a heading paraphrase, a line number — fails `sdd-task --phase`'s downstream read at execution time; a link a worker or auditor cannot resolve with `sdd-extract #` verbatim is not a valid Spec Reference. No operator stop — automated.

Step.Goal: GATE 2: operator approves the TEST PLAN.
Step.Action: Present the test plan as a decision card: each BDD scenario as a use-case, tagged `[-REQ-N]`, traced up to the scope Vision / goal it protects, plus coverage (every contract has a typing scenario, every scenario maps to a test). The operator approves **what is tested, which use-cases are covered, and that this guarantees the vision** — the one gate on substance. Out-of-scope proposals the subagent surfaced are raised here. STOP.

Step.Goal: Write the index hierarchy; hand off. (auto)
Step.Action: For each `.3-tasks.md` that does not exist yet, run `sdd-new module-index --scope --module ` to lay down the skeleton (nested `--module foo/bar` per `AX_HIERARCHICAL_SPECS`); an existing file is filled in place, never re-scaffolded. Fill per `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/module-tasks-index.xml")` (Tracker, Slug Registry, intra-module DAG, shared content per `AX_TICKET_DEDUPLICATION`). Roll up the scope tracker the same way — `sdd-new scope-index --scope ` when `.3-tasks.md` is missing, then fill per `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/scope-tasks-index.xml")` — and roll up the project index the same way — `sdd-new project-index` when `specs/3-tasks.md` is missing, then fill per `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/project-tasks-index.xml")`; never a manual `Write` of `specs/3-tasks.md` from scratch. Then run `sdd-check --all .` (task-DAG: id-collisions · deps resolve · acyclic; tracker↔ticket sync; phase graph; exec-log) and resolve or consciously defer every finding per `AX_CLOSE_WITH_INTEGRITY_CHECK` — the scaffold mutation is done only once the task graph passes. `BDD_COVERAGE` (canonical case names exist in the declared test file) gates on the ticket's own Meta Status — the existence check runs only once that ticket is `[x] DONE`, never for a freshly-scaffolded `[ ] TODO` ticket (whose test files do not exist yet by design), so a clean `sdd-check --all .` right after this step is expected, not a sign the check is silently skipped. Fix only structural findings at this step (id collisions, unresolved deps, cycles, tracker drift, broken `](…spec.md)` links) — a BDD/test-existence finding here would mean a ticket was mis-marked DONE before its tests exist, a scaffold defect worth fixing on its own, not phase noise to suppress. These trackers and tickets are read by execute with no memory of this scaffolding run — every DAG edge, rule reference, and BDD scenario must already be in the file (`AX_STATELESS_ARTIFACT`). Emit a created-files summary with traceability links. Hand off to execute (isolated, cheaper model). No operator stop.

ChatProtocol.Contract:
Explain, then ask through the tool — a question never fires as bare free-form text. A `### 💡 <О чём решаем>` section header names the decision in plain words (no `Q` numbering, no semantic question IDs); under it, ordinary language explains the question BEFORE any tool call fires — the context, the real options, and a recommendation gated by `AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND` (low-stakes: a direct pick is fine; high-stakes / architecture: do not pre-anchor one option — lay out the strongest candidates, a tail one included, or pair the recommendation with its strongest rival and the reason it might win instead). Only once the explanation stands does `AskUserQuestion` fire; its option list mirrors the printed order, short labels only — the argument itself lives in the message, never moved into the tool call.
Batching rule: one `AskUserQuestion` call may carry several questions ONLY when they are mutually independent — answering one does not change the meaning or the options of another (several facets of one single complex decision qualify as one batched call). Dependent questions, and any interview sequence, go one call at a time: compose the next question only after the previous answer is in.
Channel: use `AskUserQuestion` whenever the tool is available. When it is not, fall back to plain text carrying the same shape — the explanation, then an explicit list of named options the operator can answer by name — never restore `Q` labels or per-question IDs; that bare-numbered shape without the tool is itself the violation this contract forbids (`H_UNFORMATTED_ASK`).
Low-stakes — a recommendation is allowed, but only as the result of `AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND` (not the first typical answer):
### 💡 Формат хранения токенов Нужно решить, где держать design-токены: сгенерированный JSON проще парсить скриптам, а TS-модуль даёт автокомплит в IDE — для одного пакета без внешних потребителей разница небольшая. ✅ **JSON-файл** `[tokens.json]` — проще парсить любым языком, ничего специфичного для TS. Иначе: - **TS-модуль** `[tokens.ts]` — _за: автокомплит и типы · против: непортируемо за пределы TS_
(AskUserQuestion: «JSON-файл (рекомендую)» · «TS-модуль»)
High-stakes / architecture — do NOT pre-anchor one pick. List the strongest candidates (include a non-obvious / tail one) with «за / против» and let the operator choose; or give a recommendation only alongside its strongest alternative and the reason it might win:
### 💡 Стратегия миграции v1→v2 Три пути дают разный профиль риска и времени простоя, и откат стоит по-разному в каждом. - **Big-bang** `[migrate-all]` — _за: один переход, нет промежуточного состояния · против: долгий простой, откат дорогой_ - **Постепенная миграция по скоупам** `[migrate-incremental]` — _за: откат дешёвый, риск размазан во времени · против: два формата сосуществуют дольше_ - **Parallel-run с shadow-чтением** `[migrate-shadow]` — нетипичный вариант, но снимает риск отката почти полностью ценой временной инфраструктуры
(AskUserQuestion: «Big-bang» · «Постепенная миграция» · «Parallel-run (нетипичный)»)
A plain binary question needs no list — recommendation + inline alternative, still explained before the call:
### 💡 Нужен ли отдельный interface-скоуп Все текущие потребители — web; про API и будущих клиентов явно не говорили. ✅ **Пока не выделять** — можно добавить позже без миграции. _или сразу выделить, если API уже в планах?_
(AskUserQuestion: «Пока не выделять (рекомендую)» · «Выделить сразу»)
A counter-question in reply to a gate is a side-dive, not a rejection: (a) answer the counter-question in full, on its own merits, before returning to the gate; (b) bring the gate back exactly once, marked as a repeat pass, enriched with whatever the counter-question surfaced — «повторяю вопрос» plus a fact or option the side-dive added (e.g. operator asked "как ты делаешь ресёрч?" → the repeat pass adds an option «сначала ресёрч, потом решаем»); a verbatim repeat of the first gate carries no delta and is itself the violation. (c) if the operator answers the repeat pass with another counter-question instead of a pick, do not fire a third pass — stop and ask directly what is blocking the decision.

SddScaffold.ChatOutput:
Service line — dim, internal, kept silent (per `AX_NO_PROCESS_NARRATION`): `📋 TS_R · · · conf=`. Breadcrumb milestones (per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`): Intake · Cascade · DAG · Tickets · Tests · Done. Only two milestones are operator gates — DAG (breakdown) and Tests (test plan).
A step-boundary / decision message (the decision card) is sectioned with markdown headers, in this order. Skip any section empty for this step. During free dialogue inside a step the agent does NOT print this layout — it just talks.
`` — internal anchor + scope + mode + confidence (supplied by the branch)
`` — per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`, its OWN paragraph (a blank line above it, not just a `\n`) — markdown collapses a single newline into a space, so without the blank line the breadcrumb visually fuses onto the service line
## `` `` — одной фразой, что делаем
### 🤔 Как я понял задачу — per `UNDERSTANDING_BLOCK_FORMAT` (goes at the TOP) ### 🎯 Главное решение — the crux in plain words; add a diagram per `FLOW_DIAGRAM_WHEN` if it is a flow ### 💡 <О чём решаем> — per `QUESTION_FORMAT` ### ↓ Детали — по желанию — reasoning, full comparison, change-list (per `AX_PROGRESSIVE_DISCLOSURE`)
Glyph dictionary — closed inventory, one assigned meaning each, never a free pick. Every glyph here is chosen to read clearly on BOTH a light and a dark terminal/chat theme — half-tone shading characters (`░ ▒ ▓` and similar) are forbidden anywhere in this layout: they render as near-invisible or vanish outright depending on theme.
Section-header glyphs (fixed, one per header, in the order above): - `🤔` — the agent's own understanding check, at the top of a decision card - `🎯` — the crux decision, in plain words - `💡` — a decision the agent is proposing for the operator to confirm or pick between - `↓` — folded detail, expand on demand
Step-TYPE glyphs (fixed, keyed by the step's TYPE, used in the service line / breadcrumb, never a free pick): - `🏗` — creation / scaffold (new spec, new tickets, new files) - `🔍` — audit / review (fresh-eyes read, no write) - `🔧` — fix / reconcile (spec ⟷ code drift repair) - `⚡` — execute (a task ticket's phases running) - `🗺` — routing / overview (intent classification, project-level map)
Breadcrumb-status glyphs (per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`): `✅` done · `👷` active · `◻️` not yet.
No other emoji appear in message or section headers — the glyphs enumerated above are the only ones this layout permits.
One line, its own paragraph below the service line — a blank line separates the two (per `MESSAGE_LAYOUT`); a single `\n` with no blank line is a contract defect, markdown renders it fused onto the service line as one run-on. This session's milestones, each rendered ` `, with a status marker chosen for legibility on BOTH light and dark themes — no half-tone shading characters (`░ ▒ ▓`) anywhere, they vanish depending on theme. Status set: `✅` done · `👷` active (the step running now) · `◻️` not yet reached. Delta only; never re-list everything already settled. This is the «where are we», and it replaces a verbose run-on of finished steps.
`Vision ✅ · Scope Graph 👷 · Infra ◻️ · Portal ◻️`
The agent's compressed read of the task — its own confirmation of blind spots so the operator can catch a misread. A `### 🤔 Как я понял задачу` section near the TOP, then an italic blockquote, 2–3 sentences: the essence + the single riskiest assumption, with the assumption linked to the question that resolves it BY WORDING — there are no question numbers or IDs left to point at, so name the question itself. Never a restate of settled content.
### 🤔 Как я понял задачу > квинтэссенция — что считаю главным. > **Где могу ошибаться:** самое хрупкое допущение — это вопрос «<формулировка вопроса>».
A sub-topic dive inside a step collapses to two lines, not a five-field Return Summary:
→ ушли в `<тема>` ← `<итог одной фразой>`
When a decision is about a flow — data moving, state transitions, start / stop conditions — draw a tiny ASCII diagram; one glance beats a paragraph. This is the one place a fenced block is allowed inside an operator message (alignment matters). Keep it small.
``` [сеть] [auth] [конфиг] ──всё есть──► ОПРОС идёт ▲ │ └──── снова есть ──── ПАУЗА ◄───────┘ что-то пропало ```
Decision first, reasoning on demand. The must-read top of a message is short: where we are + my read + what to decide. Everything heavy — full option comparison, evidence, the change-list, derivations — goes BELOW a `### ↓ Детали — по желанию` header. Never dump reasoning above the questions. Facts already verified collapse to one line («сверился: …»); uncertainties that need the operator BECOME the questions — never list them twice.

ArtifactOutput.Contract:
One line per entry — no Status/Recorded fields, no multi-line block. The parenthetical carries only what applies; omit a clause entirely rather than writing it empty.
```markdown D-NNN — (почему: ; отвергнуто: ; риск: ) ```
Superseding a prior decision appends `; supersedes: D-MMM` to the parenthetical instead of a separate field — the entry stays one line. `` is the recording date (`YYYY-MM-DD`); status (active / superseded / rejected / deferred) is implicit from prose and from whether a later entry supersedes this one — a spec has no dangling "rejected" or "deferred" entries sitting as if active, the prose says so directly (e.g. `отвергнуто в пользу X` folded into the same line that would have recorded it, never a standalone rejected entry with its own D-NNN).
